general.rule: FIFA conducts a fair play contest based on an appraisal of team conduct by a FIFA delegate.
The objective is to foster a sporting spirit among players, team officials and spectators.
After each match, the delegate completes the fair play form after consulting the referee and referee assessor.
Every match in the final competition is taken into account.
FIFA compiles and publishes the final classification; its decision is final.
The winning association receives a football-related social-development campaign with a budget of up to USD 50,000.

cards.name: Red and yellow cards
cards.calculation: Start at 10 points and subtract the applicable deductions.
cards.note: This is the only criterion that can entail minus points.

positive_play.name: Positive play
positive_aspects: Continuing to attempt to score even after the desired result has effectively been achieved
positive_play.note: Positive play is generally correlated with scoring chances created and goals scored.

respect_opponent.name: Respect towards the opponent
respect_opponent.note: Avoid duplicating the card assessment; focus on positive attitudes such as helping an injured opponent.

respect_match_officials.name: Respect towards the referee/match officials
respect_match_officials.note: Acceptance of decisions without protest should be rewarded.

team_officials.name: Behaviour of the team officials
team_officials.note: Includes sporting, technical, tactical and ethical conduct, calming players, acceptance of decisions and media cooperation.

crowd.name: Behaviour of the crowd
crowd.note: Use n.a. when the number of supporting fans is negligible; in that case the maximum match total is 35 instead of 40.

final_assessment.formula: (sum of criterion points / maximum possible points) * 1000
final_assessment.overall_competition_score: Average of the match assessments over the number of matches played.

eligibility.rule: Teams eliminated after the group stage are excluded from the fair play contest.
